content: Do not take candesartan and hydrochlorothiazide if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as it may harm the fetus. Candesartan and hydrochlorothiazide are prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. Candesartan belongs to a class of drugs called angiotensin II receptor antagonists, which work by relaxing blood vessels and improving blood flow by blocking certain natural chemicals that tighten the vessels. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, or water pill, that helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt through urine. This medication is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once or twice daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. While candesartan and hydrochlorothiazide help control high blood pressure, they do not cure it. It may take up to four weeks to experience the full benefits. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before taking candesartan and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to candesartan (Atacand), hydrochlorothiazide (HydroDIURIL, Microzide), sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention medications such as aspirin, NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), cholestyramine, colestipol, lithium, diabetes medications, narcotic pain relievers, oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, prednisone), other blood pressure medications, phenobarbital, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are on dialysis or have a history of allergies, asthma, lupus, diabetes, heart failure, gout, or kidney or liver disease. Let your doctor know if you plan to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform the surgeon or dentist that you are taking this medication. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can exacerbate side effects. Be aware that candesartan and hydrochlorothiazide may cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, especially when standing up quickly from a lying position. This is more common when starting the medication. To minimize this, rise slowly and rest your feet on the floor for a few moments before standing. Additionally, diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, and excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet or an exercise program, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Candesartan and hydrochlorothiazide may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience dizziness or back pain. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include lightheadedness, fainting, dry mouth, thirst, weakness, fatigue, drowsiness, restlessness, confusion, seizures, muscle pain or cramps, infrequent urination, rapid or pounding heartbeat, upset stomach, or vomiting. Report any unusual problems to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be ordered to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
